relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a GFAP variant carrier: "We report on a 56-year-old man who was genetically confirmed as AOAD with the glial fibrillary acidic protein mutation of p.M74T"; the Discussion also gives individual-level facts (variant, Japanese, middle-aged, dysarthria and dysphagia) for one previously published patient (ref [6]).
method_note: Hand extraction from the text; the JSON was assembled by a short Python script in the scratch directory (all values typed from my reading, no table transcription; the paper has no tables). Two in-scope people: the case patient ('patient', rule 5) and the previously published patient of ref [6] ('ref [6] patient', rule 4; in scope under v4 because the paper gives variant p.M74T, 'middle-aged', 'Japanese' and dysarthria/dysphagia for that person). The paper states 'this gene mutation has been reported only in two AOAD patients' (including ours). Variant printed only as protein shorthand 'p.M74T'; no cDNA, transcript, zygosity, inheritance or parental testing given; authors call it a 'mutation' only, so pathogenicity and variant type are 'not reported'. n_patients_reported = 1 for the case described first-hand; the ref [6] patient is a prior report. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (paper does not say its patient was described before). 'Dysarthria and dysphagia were not obvious' / 'without apparent dysarthria and dysphagia' recorded as excluded (hedged wording; the Discussion adds that bulbar palsy was 'not obvious' and the increased masseter reflex 'may imply potential pseudobulbar palsy'). 'palatal myoclonus was not observed' mapped to checklist 'palatal tremor' excluded. Normal findings per D-27: 'superficial sensation was normal' -> decreased superficial sensation excluded; normal N20 latency -> prolonged N20 latency excluded. Whole-investigation normals ('Blood examination revealed no particular abnormalities', 'Cerebrospinal fluid study results were normal', 'Nerve conduction study results were normal') recorded as written and exclude nothing more specific. 'mild cognitive impairment' (MMSE 21/28) mapped to checklist 'cognitive decline' observed ('He developed mild cognitive impairment'). 'cerebellar ocular symptoms' (saccadic pursuit, gaze-evoked nystagmus) mapped to 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' observed. The abstract says 'sensory disturbances in four limbs' while the case presentation describes sensory symptoms in the legs only; both recorded as stated. Pons/midbrain/cerebrum 'not atrophied' do not exclude the basal ganglia/thalamic checklist item (narrow vs broad). General Discussion statements (e.g. medullary atrophy 'present in all patients with AOAD') were not applied to the ref [6] patient. No contradictions found within the paper.
